text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

Before I draft, there's one problem to raise and a few questions.

**The "same cleaner every single time" promise.** Your own numbers don't support it. 7 of your 18 cleaners left last year, and your fix is a regular cleaner plus a named backup. That's a good fix, but it isn't a guarantee. These readers left partly because the cleaner kept changing. If you promise "every single time" and someone sees a new face by visit three, you've proven their reason for leaving and you probably won't get a second chance. What you can honestly promise is still strong: "You'll have one regular cleaner, and if they're ever out, a backup you've already met, never a stranger." I'd write it that way unless you tell me something that makes the stronger version true.

Questions, most important first:

1. **What's changed on cleaner turnover?** Have you raised pay, changed hiring, or seen fewer people leave this year? Any concrete sign that cleaners stay longer now would back up the backup promise better than anything else.
2. **Does the backup actually meet the customer?** For example, does the backup do an intro visit or sometimes cover a visit? Or is it just a name on file?
3. **What happens after the $99 cleaning?** Does it go back to $165, or is there any returning-customer rate? Is there a contract or minimum commitment? Is there a deadline for the offer?
4. **Can you commit to something if it goes wrong?** For example: if an unfamiliar cleaner shows up, that visit is free or discounted. Or: you'll tell the customer ahead of time whenever their cleaner changes.
5. **Who signs it, and will you use names?** Can the email include the customer's first name and the name of their former cleaner, if that cleaner still works for you?
6. **Anything they'll find out anyway?** Has the price gone up since they left, or is there a fee, a waitlist, or a limit on which areas or slots are open?

Once you answer (or tell me you don't know), I'll write the roughly 150-word email.

You're right, I can't promise every single time because of sick days and holidays. Go with your wording, as strong as it can be while staying true.

1. Since we started giving each customer a regular cleaner in July, 1 of our 18 cleaners has left. I don't know of any pay or hiring changes beyond that.
2. I don't know.
3. I don't know what the price is after the $99 cleaning. There's no contract, and customers can cancel any time. The offer ends December 31.
4. The only thing I can commit to is a regular cleaner and a named backup for every customer. I don't know about anything beyond that.
5. Sign it from me, Lisa Grant, owner of Brightway Home Cleaning. I don't know about using the customer's or cleaner's names.
6. I don't know.

I used the wording we agreed on. The email promises a regular cleaner and a named backup, not the same cleaner every single time.

<final_document>
Subject: Your own cleaner, and a $99 cleaning to come back

Hi,

When customers left Brightway last year, the two reasons we heard most were price and a different cleaner showing up too often. You were right about the cleaners, and we've fixed it.

Since July, every customer has their own regular cleaner, plus a named backup for sick days and holidays. You'll always know who's coming to your home. Since we made that change, 1 of our 18 cleaners has left.

About price: yes, we cost more than the app services. Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay them $21 an hour, and every visit is insured.

If you come back, your first cleaning is $99. There's no contract, and you can cancel any time. This offer ends December 31.

Just reply to this email and we'll match you with your regular cleaner.

Lisa Grant
Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning
</final_document>

A few things to know before you send it:

- **The price after the $99 cleaning isn't in the email** because you didn't know it. Since price was the top reason people left, many readers will want to know before they reply. If you can add a line like "after that, your regular price is $X," the email gets stronger. Even an honest "$165 every other week for a 3-bedroom" beats leaving them to guess.
- **I didn't say the backup is someone they've already met.** You didn't know that. If it is true, add it, because it's the best answer to "a stranger in my house."
- **"1 of 18 has left since July" covers about four months.** That's true and worth saying, but it isn't a full year. I didn't claim that turnover is solved.
- **I didn't link your pay to cleaners staying.** You paid $21 last year too, when 7 left, so the email presents pay and insurance as what the higher price buys, not as the reason cleaners stay.
- **Personalisation:** if you can merge in first names, use "Hi [First name]," instead of "Hi,".
